text:
Ben: Heads-up — eviction rate in eu-west3 preemptible pool jumped to ~21% in the last 30m, baseline ~3%. Graph: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/evictions/eu-west3?from=now-30m
Alice: On it. Which pool id? mixed-gpu-medium or the heterogeneous one?
Ben: mixed-gpu-medium-2. I filtered by pool tag in the dashboard.
Carmen: I noticed churn earlier around 09:12 UTC where autoscaler removed nodes then re-added. Might be scaling loop + network blips.
Dinesh: Looking at node logs now — a bunch of kernel OOM_killer activity on a subset of hosts, then they get preempted by the cloud provider. Could be related but odd.
Ben: PromQL I used: ```sum(rate(eviction_total{region="eu-west3", pool="mixed-gpu-medium-2"}[5m])) by (instance)``` shows the spike concentrated on 4 hosts.
Alice: I created a quick alert tweak to reduce noise (10m window) and pinned the panel. @deploy-bot can you open an incident for tracking? :eyes:
deploy-bot: Incident created — INC-3412. Priority: p2. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-3412
Carmen: Proposal: enable short hedging (0.15) for mixed-gpu-medium-2 and temporarily increase on-demand fallback capacity by 8 instances. That should reduce request failures while we root-cause. Thoughts?
Dinesh: +1 to hedging. Also will run the connectivity probe against the 4 suspect hosts to rule out NIC flaps.
Ben: I'll patch the capacity manager for a 15m override to spin up 8 on-demand. Pushing change in 2m.
Alice: I'll add a dashboard row comparing eviction_rate, kernel_ooms, and network_errors for those instances. If kern_oom correlates, we may need a host image rollback.
Carmen: If this repeats after hedging we should consider marking the whole AZ as degraded and shift traffic. Don't want cascading retries.
Dinesh: Probe results — two hosts show >20% packet_loss for a 3m window right before evictions. Filing infra ticket with cloud provider.
Ben: Mitigation applied: hedging=0.15, +8 on-demand brought capacity back to target. Eviction rate dropped to ~4% within 10m.
Alice: Nice. Incident notes: root-cause hypothesis = transient NIC degradation leading to VM instability -> kernel OOMs -> provider preemptions. Next steps: collect full host traces, repro attempt in staging, provider support case.
Carmen: I'll own post-incident write-up and add remediation options (auto-evict noisy hosts earlier, better NIC telemetry).
Ben: Thanks all. If anyone sees a secondary blip tag this thread. :thumbsup:
